designs.title: Probably Fine
designs.why: Tight 4x5 grid with icons drawn at one stroke weight, and a heavy grotesk punchline that anchors the bottom. It has the clean hierarchy of a spec sheet and reads as a unit from across a room. The tracked condensed labels are crisp, but at print size they become texture. Some glyphs (glow plug, door open) are weak silhouettes, and there is a dead band of empty space under PROBABLY FINE. The deadpan joke depends on that headline, which works.
designs.fix: Close the gap under the grid and set PROBABLY FINE wider, about the full grid width (roughly 1.15x its current size), so the type and the grid share one measure. Then crop the empty space at the bottom.

designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: Lovely pairing: a tracked classical serif title, italic serif captions and loose brush dogs, all in one consistent hand. The repeated 'Turn around.' gives the eye a rhythm, and the curled dog in 7 resolves it well. The composition is too airy, though. The gutters between columns are wider than the drawings, so on the tee it breaks into small isolated vignettes rather than one block. The dogs are small next to the empty space, and the moon floats alone.
designs.fix: Tighten the two columns toward the centre and scale the dogs up about 25%, so the seven steps lock into a compact block under the title. Captions stay the same size.

designs.title: The Box
designs.why: A wordless three-beat gag in clean, confident line art. The cat's tail in 2 and the bed in 3 breaking the panel frame is a nice compositional touch, and the payoff panel reads instantly. As a layout it is a narrow vertical strip pushed left by the heavy numerals, so on the tee it sits as a thin off-centre column. Those bold grotesk numerals are louder than anything inside the panels. The dense tabby striping will close up in one-ink print at small size.
designs.fix: Reduce the numerals to roughly the panel line weight (or tuck them inside the panel corners) and centre the strip on the panels themselves. That removes the left-heavy imbalance and leaves the cat as the loudest element.
